objects.name: SSP Brick (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Construct a SSP (Stabilized Single Point) Brick element from an eight vertex mesh.
The mesh is reordered into the node order OpenSees wants and checked for a positive Jacobian at every corner - a brick wound the wrong way round, or twisted, is one the solver accepts and answers with the wrong sign rather than rejecting.

A solid has no local axes. OpenSees gives neither element an orientation argument, and an nD material has no orientation either, so the material's own directions - Ex, Ey and Ez on an Elastic Orthotropic - are the global X, Y and Z, and so are the stresses read back. To align an orthotropic material with the part, rotate the model.
Where a solid meets a beam or a shell at a point, the two are tied in translation only: a solid node carries no moment, so the junction is a pin.

objects.name: Construct Point
objects.desc: Construct a point from {xyz} coordinates.

objects.name: Support (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
A support. Rigid: fixes the node along and about the axes of the Position's plane you choose. Elastic: a spring along or about each axis of the plane. Compression Only: holds the node only while it pushes into the support, along the plane's Z, and lets it lift - after a gap, if there is one.
Elastic and Compression Only never fix the node themselves, so a Rigid support on the same point can hold what they leave free: a pinned bearing that can lift is a Compression Only support with a Rigid one holding Tx and Ty only.
Reaction Force gives a spring support a row of its own, with the spring's force.

objects.name: Topology Optimisation (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Finds where a solid needs its material. Method picks how: SIMP (the default) gives every solid a density and finds the stiffest design for VolumeFraction of the material, as top3d; BESO starts from every solid and takes a few percent of the volume away each iteration, each element solid or void all along; Multi-Material finds where each of several materials goes, and where none is needed. Right click the component, Method, to switch; the inputs and outputs change with it, and a switch starts any run again.
The solids of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - are the design domain. A removed element keeps a billionth of its stiffness instead of being cut out, so the mesh never changes. Every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. Set Run to true to start; the outputs follow the run as it goes.
Once it stops, AlpacaModel is the design as a model of its own, to analyse.

SIMP: Finds where a solid needs its material. Every solid of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - gets a density between 0 and 1 and a stiffness of density cubed, and the densities are found that make the model stiffest under its loads with VolumeFraction of the material: SIMP with the optimality criteria update and a density filter, as top3d. Removed material is never cut out: a void element keeps a billionth of its stiffness, so the mesh stays as it is.
Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), on the same nodes, because an SSP Brick fixes part of its stiffness when it is built. Every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. Beams, shells and links in the model take no part: they keep their full stiffness. One OpenSees stays open for the whole run.
Set Run to true to start. The outputs follow the run as it goes. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped, and so does a run given more Iterations or a smaller Tolerance after it ended. Changing any other input starts it again from the beginning.
Once it stops, AlpacaModel is the design as a model of its own, solid and void, to analyse.

BESO: Finds where a solid needs its material by BESO, bi-directional evolutionary structural optimisation. It starts from every solid of the model and takes EvolutionRate of the volume away each iteration, until VolumeFraction is left: each iteration keeps the elements that work hardest - their strain energy per volume, smoothed over FilterRadius and averaged with the iteration before - and lets the rest go, or brings void ones back. Every element is solid or void all along, so every iteration is a design of its own, of the volume reached: drag Step to look through them.
A void element keeps a billionth of its stiffness instead of being cut out, so the mesh stays as it is. Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), and every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material, as in Topology Optimisation. The run stops once the volume is reached and the compliance has settled: the last five iterations' within Tolerance of the five before.
Set Run to true to start. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped. Changing any input but Iterations and Tolerance starts it again from the beginning.

Multi-Material: Finds where each of several materials goes in a solid, and where none is needed: the design stiffest under the model's loads with each material filling at most its share of the volume. Every solid of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - gets a density of every material, and its stiffness mixes the materials' Young's moduli so that an element of one material alone pays least: the mapping-based interpolation of Zheng, Yi, Peng and Yoon (2024), with a density filter, a projection that grows sharper every 50 iterations, and MMA, as they do.
Only the materials' Young's moduli count: every solid keeps the Poisson's ratio of its own material, and only stiffness is optimised, so a material strong in tension goes where its stiffness pays, not where the tension is.
Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), as in Topology Optimisation, and every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. The solids in Keep stay as modelled.
Set Run to true to start. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped. Changing any input but Iterations and Tolerance starts it again from the beginning.

Method picks how: SIMP (the default) gives every solid a density and finds the stiffest design for VolumeFraction of the material, as top3d; BESO starts from every solid and takes a few percent of the volume away each iteration, each element solid or void all along; Multi-Material finds where each of several materials goes, and where none is needed. Right click the component, Method, to switch; the inputs and outputs change with it, and a switch starts any run again.
The solids of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - are the design domain. A removed element keeps a billionth of its stiffness instead of being cut out, so the mesh never changes. Every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. Set Run to true to start; the outputs follow the run as it goes.
Once it stops, AlpacaModel is the design as a model of its own, to analyse.

SIMP: Finds where a solid needs its material. Every solid of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - gets a density between 0 and 1 and a stiffness of density cubed, and the densities are found that make the model stiffest under its loads with VolumeFraction of the material: SIMP with the optimality criteria update and a density filter, as top3d. Removed material is never cut out: a void element keeps a billionth of its stiffness, so the mesh stays as it is.
Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), on the same nodes, because an SSP Brick fixes part of its stiffness when it is built. Every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. Beams, shells and links in the model take no part: they keep their full stiffness. One OpenSees stays open for the whole run.
Set Run to true to start. The outputs follow the run as it goes. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped, and so does a run given more Iterations or a smaller Tolerance after it ended. Changing any other input starts it again from the beginning.
Once it stops, AlpacaModel is the design as a model of its own, solid and void, to analyse.

BESO: Finds where a solid needs its material by BESO, bi-directional evolutionary structural optimisation. It starts from every solid of the model and takes EvolutionRate of the volume away each iteration, until VolumeFraction is left: each iteration keeps the elements that work hardest - their strain energy per volume, smoothed over FilterRadius and averaged with the iteration before - and lets the rest go, or brings void ones back. Every element is solid or void all along, so every iteration is a design of its own, of the volume reached: drag Step to look through them.
A void element keeps a billionth of its stiffness instead of being cut out, so the mesh stays as it is. Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), and every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material, as in Topology Optimisation. The run stops once the volume is reached and the compliance has settled: the last five iterations' within Tolerance of the five before.
Set Run to true to start. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped. Changing any input but Iterations and Tolerance starts it again from the beginning.

Multi-Material: Finds where each of several materials goes in a solid, and where none is needed: the design stiffest under the model's loads with each material filling at most its share of the volume. Every solid of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - gets a density of every material, and its stiffness mixes the materials' Young's moduli so that an element of one material alone pays least: the mapping-based interpolation of Zheng, Yi, Peng and Yoon (2024), with a density filter, a projection that grows sharper every 50 iterations, and MMA, as they do.
Only the materials' Young's moduli count: every solid keeps the Poisson's ratio of its own material, and only stiffness is optimised, so a material strong in tension goes where its stiffness pays, not where the tension is.
Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), as in Topology Optimisation, and every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. The solids in Keep stay as modelled.
Set Run to true to start. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped. Changing any input but Iterations and Tolerance starts it again from the beginning.

objects.text:
Topology Optimisation: top3d's benchmarks, three ways.

Two problems of top3d (Liu and Tovar 2014, 'An efficient 3D topology optimization code written in Matlab'), in its units. SIMP runs with top3d's settings: 30% of the volume, penalty 3, a filter radius of 1.5, at most 200 iterations; the panels give what Alpaca4d's test bench and a numpy port of top3d give for the same problems. Beside it, BESO carves the block down to the same 30%, every brick solid or void, and Multi-Material shares the 30% between the unit material (18%) and one half as stiff (12%); both with the filter radius of 1.5 too.

1. Set Run Cantilever to true: its three runs go together, each on its own thread, and the designs draw one above the other as they go - SIMP at the top, BESO, and Multi-Material where the model is.
2. SIMP ends after 200 iterations: neither problem reaches top3d's tolerance of 0.01 before then; nor does top3d. Compare 'Compliance, last iteration' with the panels beside it. The first iterations agree with top3d to round-off; the cantilever's runs part by up to 0.2% while its design rearranges itself around iteration 70, and come back together.
3. The same for the simply supported beam, with Run Simply supported.
4. Drag a Step slider back to watch the problem's runs again, design by design: every iteration is kept.

Expected from SIMP: the cantilever as top flange, bottom flange and diagonal webs; the simply supported beam as a truss, its tie thickest at mid-span. Topology Optimisation needs a license.
